similar: Jonathan Richman And The Modern Lovers
info.bio:
The Modern Lovers fue una banda de rock estadounidense liderada por Jonathan Richman, que funcionó durante los años setenta y ochenta.

La primera época de la banda va del año 1970 a 1974. Sus grabaciones aparecieron años después y fueron muy influyentes. El disco homónimo de la banda (1976), contiene temas como "Roadrunner", "She Cracked" o "Hospital", que pueden ser considerados clásicos.

El sonido de la banda parece estar influenciado por The Velvet Underground

scenes.name: Decadencia y glam-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El rock siempre tuvo un elemento de decadencia, amoralidad y obscenidad; entre los Cockettes (1968) y el Rocky Horror Picture Show (1974) se convierte en producto de masas. Gran Bretaña lo llama glam-rock: T.Rex lo inaugura y lo casa con el hard rock; David Bowie lo lleva a su cima comercial convirtiendo el marketing en arte (Ziggy Stardust, la trilogía berlinesa con Eno). En EE UU, Alice Cooper, Sparks, Iggy Pop y Lou Reed (Berlin, Metal Machine Music, New York). El glam y la decadencia preparan el punk: Mott The Hoople, Be Bop Deluxe, New York Dolls, Heartbreakers, Dictators, Modern Lovers de Jonathan Richman, Runaways.

podcast.title: Obscurity and Breakup
podcast.body: The Modern Lovers, fronted by Jonathan Richman, toiled in obscurity for several years. Despite their distinctive sound, which was ahead of its time, they did not achieve widespread recognition. The band ultimately broke up in 1974. "Jonathan and his band, the modern lovers, toiled in obscurity for a couple of years before breaking up in 1974."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Breakup Success of Members
podcast.body: Following the band's dissolution in 1974, two of its members went on to achieve greater success. Drummer David Robertson found work with another Boston group, The Cars. Keyboardist Jerry Harrison joined the new band The Talking Heads. Both The Cars and The Talking Heads would later become significant components of the American New Wave era. "However, two members of the band went on to bigger and better things. Drummer David Robertson found work with another Boston group called The Cars and Keyboard is Jerry Harrison soon hooked up with a new band called The Talking Heads."

xref.title: Contribution to New Wave
xref.body: The Cars, featuring former Modern Lovers drummer David Robertson, became a major component of the American New Wave era. This highlights the post-breakup success of members from The Modern Lovers. "And both the talking heads and the cars would eventually become major components of the American New Wave era."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Obscurity and Band Breakup
xref.body: Jonathan Richman and his band, The Modern Lovers, worked in obscurity for a couple of years after recording demos like "Roadrunner" in 1971. Despite the forward-thinking nature of their music, the timing was not right for their style to gain widespread recognition. The band eventually broke up in 1974. "Jonathan and his band, the modern lovers, toiled in obscurity for a couple of years before breaking up in 1974."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Groundwork for Punk Rock
xref.body: The stripped-down songs of Jonathan Richman and The Modern Lovers were instrumental in laying the groundwork for punk rock, with their music frequently classified as proto-punk, meaning it predated and helped define the genre. "His stripped down songs help set the groundwork for punk rock. In fact, we classify his music as proto-punk, the stuff that had to happen first before punk rock could be born."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

xref.title: Influence on Punk and Post-Punk
xref.body: Although Jonathan Richman and the Modern Lovers never achieved significant record sales, they were highly influential to early punk bands and many post-punk groups such as the Sex Pistols, R.E.M., Violent Femmes, Dinosaur Jr., The Cars, The Pixies, and the Ramones. This impact stemmed from Jonathan Richman being a big Velvet Underground fan. "Jonathan Richmond and the Modern Lovers never sold a lot of records, but they were very important to the early punks and many of the post-punk bands like the Sex Pistols and REM and the Violent Femmes and Dinosaur Jr. and the Cars and the Pixies and the Ramones."
